flags.description: Credit Suisse agreed in 2021 to pay roughly $475–547 million combined to US and UK authorities (including a $100 million SEC settlement) over fraud and FCPA violations in Mozambique's 'tuna bonds' scandal, where bankers received $50 million in hidden kickbacks for arranging loans nominally meant for a state tuna-fishing fleet and coast guard.

Following the March 2021 collapse of Archegos Capital, which cost Credit Suisse $5.5 billion, an independent review found the losses resulted from a fundamental failure of management and controls; the UK's PRA fined the bank £87 million in 2023 and Swiss regulator FINMA found Credit Suisse had 'seriously and systematically' breached financial market laws.
